Their first home match away from it was played at the [Nikos Goumas Stadium](/wiki/Nikos_Goumas_Stadium "Nikos Goumas Stadium") in 1962, and the Karaiskakis Stadium was used for the first time in 1964 after it was renovated. Main article: [Cambridge University (UK Parliament constituency)](/wiki/Cambridge_University_(UK_Parliament_constituency) "Cambridge University (UK Parliament constituency)")

See also: [Category:Members of the Parliament of the United Kingdom for the University of Cambridge](/wiki/Category:Members_of_the_Parliament_of_the_United_Kingdom_for_the_University_of_Cambridge "Category:Members of the Parliament of the United Kingdom for the University of Cambridge")

The University of Cambridge was one of only two universities to hold parliamentary seats in the [Parliament of England](/wiki/Parliament_of_England "Parliament of England") and was later one of 19 represented in the [Parliament of the United Kingdom](/wiki/Parliament_of_the_United_Kingdom "Parliament of the United Kingdom"). The constituency was created by a [Royal charter](/wiki/Royal_charter "Royal charter") of 1603 and returned two members of parliament until 1950 when it was abolished by the [Representation of the People Act 1948](/wiki/Representation_of_the_People_Act_1948 "Representation of the People Act 1948"). The constituency was not a geographical area; rather, its electorate consisted of university graduates. Before 1918, the franchise was restricted to male graduates with a [doctorate](/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy "Doctor of Philosophy") or [MA](/wiki/Master_of_Arts_(Oxbridge_and_Dublin) "Master of Arts (Oxbridge and Dublin)") degree.

OPEC's [international aid](/wiki/International_aid "International aid") activities date from well before the 1973–1974 oil price surge. For example, the [Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development](/wiki/Kuwait_Fund_for_Arab_Economic_Development "Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development") has operated since 1961.[[73]](#cite_note-73)

In the years after 1973, as an example of so-called "[checkbook diplomacy](/wiki/Checkbook_diplomacy "Checkbook diplomacy")", certain Arab nations have been among the world's largest providers of foreign aid,[[74]](#cite_note-74)[[75]](#cite_note-75) and OPEC added to its goals the selling of oil for the socio-economic growth of poorer nations. The OPEC Special Fund was conceived in [Algiers, Algeria](/wiki/Algiers,_Algeria "Algiers, Algeria"), in March 1975, and was established in January 1976.[[76]](#cite_note-76)

"A Solemn Declaration 'reaffirmed the natural solidarity which unites OPEC countries with other developing countries in their struggle to overcome underdevelopment,' and called for measures to strengthen cooperation between these countries... [The OPEC Special Fund's] resources are additional to those already made available by OPEC states through a number of bilateral and multilateral channels."[[77]](#cite_note-77) The Fund became an official international development agency in May 1980 and was renamed the [OPEC Fund for International Development](/wiki/OPEC_Fund_for_International_Development "OPEC Fund for International Development"),[[78]](#cite_note-78) with Permanent Observer status at the United Nations.[[79]](#cite_note-79) In 2020, the institution ceased using the abbreviation OFID.

The program was reorganized in 1972; the first M.D. degrees from the new Program in Medicine were awarded to a graduating class of 58 students in 1975. In 1991, the school was officially renamed the Brown University School of Medicine, then renamed once more to Brown Medical School in October 2000.[[139]](#cite_note-147) In January 2007, entrepreneur and philanthropist [Warren Alpert](/wiki/Warren_Alpert "Warren Alpert") donated $100 million to the school. In recognition of the gift, the school's name was changed to the Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University.
